3.text: Okhotsk Sea among the Maritime Koryak.

4.text: The hunting of “resident” reindeer is done with the gun, and sometimes

5.text: even now with the bow. For instance, bucks that go to the Chukchee herds

6.text: in rutting-time may be killed only with the bow or with the lasso. The Lamut,

7.text: and, following their example, also the Reindeer Chukchee, take advantage of

8.text: the well-known curiosity of the reindeer, to lure it within shooting range by

9.text: means of a special decoy-reindeer, which is put to pasture in the open field,

10.text: on the end of a very long and thin line. When wild reindeer are espied at

11.text: a distance, the hunter hides behind some tree or large stone. The Lamut

12.text: on the open plain will crouch behind the back of his riding-reindeer. Thus

13.text: the hunter patiently awaits the oncomers, directing the course of his decoy-

14.text: animal by dexterous pulls and jerks of the line. The best decoy-animal is a

15.text: cross with a wild reindeer, — in the rutting-season a young doe, or a buck

16.text: with large antlers, that is taken by the wild bucks for a rival.

17.text: The Lamut hunt reindeer in the spring, running on snowshoes over the

18.text: hard-crusted snow, but this is possible only in a wooded country. On the

19.text: tundra the snow is always too hard-beaten by winds to give a man with

20.text: snowshoes any advantage over the reindeer.

21.text: To the Maritime Chukchee the wild reindeer cannot be so important as

22.text: to the American Eskimo, because most of the hunt is done by the Reindeer

23.text: Chukchee and other inland tribes; and the maritime people, for the most part,

24.text: can only have a share in their large hunts. Thus, as already mentioned,

25.text: people from Pacific villages in former times used to go up the Anadyr River

26.text: to take part in the reindeer-killing on the water. On the tundra between the

27.text: Anadyr and Indian Point the chief reindeer-hunters are Maritime Chukchee,

28.text: who have acquired a few reindeer, and who for this reason spend much time

29.text: inland, scouring the country the whole time far and wide. The same is true

31.text: The elk, in former times, lived in the Kolyma country, close to the

32.text: seashore; and the Kolyma Yukaghir derived from it a considerable part of

33.text: their food. Around old dwelling-places at the mouth of the Kolyma I could

34.text: always find an abundance of elk antlers and bones; and the jacket of a

35.text: Yukaghir corpse that Mr. Jochelson found in a wooden burial-box on the

36.text: lower part of the Dry Anui was made of elk-skin. In the last two centuries

37.text: the elk has retreated into the forest, and does not go to the tundra. The

38.text: Chukchee, therefore, hunt the elk but little, though in former times they were

39.text: familiar with that animal, as is indicated by the frequent use of its name.
